metadata.note: Verbatim DDInter 2.0 slice for issue #206 — the CONTRAINDICATION chip's subject label, on a family the KB lists ROUTE-QUALIFIED ROW FIRST. Rows and interaction rows are field-for-field their KB rows, in KB order, and the interaction rows are every KB pair among these drugs. Chloroprocaine is one of the shipped multi-row families whose route-unspecified row is not the family's first, so dataset order and DrugReference.canonicalRow DISAGREE here — which is what makes a contraindication chip named by the resolved subject distinguishable from one named by whichever row reached the arm first. Procaine and Tetracaine are the ALLERGENS: each is a different substance sharing ATC level-4 subgroup N01BA with chloroprocaine, so each is one class-related finding and two of them are two findings about one subject — the shape that separates renaming the chip from duplicating it. Lorazepam is the interaction partner, and its rule sits on the UNQUALIFIED chloroprocaine row only, so the interaction arm and the contraindication arm can be read against each other in one response. The Chloroprocaine (ophthalmic) x Chloroprocaine row is the KB's own self-pair for this family and is expected to be dropped at load (issue #152). This is ddi-canonical-subject-label.json's slice widened with the two allergens; that fixture carries none, and ddi-contra-route-variants.json's hydrocortisone family lists its unqualified row FIRST, so a positional subject and a resolved one agree there and a case built on it would test nothing. Widen this one rather than authoring a fourth chloroprocaine slice.

5520.text: The concomitant use of local anesthetics and benzodiazepines may have additive CNS-depressant effects. Both types of drugs are CNS depressants.

6466.text: Some topical anesthetics can be systemically absorbed and cause methemoglobinemia, particularly when applied to mucous membranes.  Coadministration with other oxidizing agents that can also induce methemoglobinemia such as injectable local anesthetics, antimalarials (e.g., chloroquine, primaquine, quinine, tafenoquine), nitrates and nitrites, sulfonamides, aminosalicylic acid, dapsone, dimethyl sulfoxide, flutamide, metoclopramide, nitrofurantoin, phenazopyridine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, and rasburicase may increase the risk.
